name: Arcology On Permafrost
description: You are given three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$k$$$, where $$$m \cdot k \lt n$$$. For a sequence $$$b$$$ consisting of non-negative integers, define $$$f(b)$$$ as follows: You may perform the following operation on $$$b$$$: Let $$$l$$$ denote the current length of $$$b$$$. Choose a positive integer $$$1 \leq i \leq l - k + 1$$$, remove the subarray from index $$$i$$$ to $$$i + k - 1$$$ and concatenate the remaining parts. In other words, replace $$$b$$$ with $$$$$$[b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{i - 1}, b_{i + k}, b_{i + k + 1}, \ldots, b_l].$$$$$$ $$$f(b)$$$ is defined as the minimum possible value of $$$\operatorname{mex}(b)$$$$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ after performing the above operation at most $$$m$$$ times (possibly zero). You need to construct a sequence $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ consisting of non-negative integers, such that: For all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$. Over all such sequences $$$a$$$, $$$f(a)$$$ is maximized . $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$The minimum excluded (MEX) of a collection of integers $$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_k$$$ is defined as the smallest non-negative integer $$$x$$$ which does not occur in the collection $$$c$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le m \lt n$$$, $$$1 \le k \lt n$$$, $$$1 \le m \cdot k \lt n$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2084D — Arcology On Permafrost [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
